Technical demo: reads the operator’s reply from the system USSD dialog after you run a saved code in this app

This app is a technical demo of the Android AccessibilityService API. Saving and dialling USSD codes (like *100#) is its example use case. This service reads the text of the operator’s reply from the system phone dialog (com.android.phone only) and presses its OK button so the dialog closes. It only does this for up to 30 seconds after you tap a code in this app. The reply is shown in the app and stored on this device only. It does not read any other app or screen, does not record what you type, and sends nothing off the device.

This app uses Android’s Accessibility Service to read USSD replies

Accessibility demo uses the AccessibilityService API to read the text of the operator’s reply in the system phone dialog that appears after you run a USSD code in this app, and to press its OK button so the dialog closes.
It only works on dialogs from the system phone app (com.android.phone), and only for up to 30 seconds after you tap a code in this app.
It does not read any other app or screen, does not record what you type, and does not collect passwords or personal data.
The reply text is saved only on this device and shown in the app. Nothing is sent anywhere.
You can turn the service off at any time in Settings → Accessibility. If you decline, you can still dial your codes, but replies will not be captured and shown in the app.
